answer: Before any bucket is drawn the rope is lowered and its knots counted against the well's own depth, and the well keeper writes the count in the book. A ember rope knotted at home fails the gauge: at the forge of the well the knots must match the depth the keeper measured, and a home rope is knotted blind. Faking a gauge means digging a false well, bribing a keeper and paying 9,400, while the comet tally in the well book is read at every drawing, so a rope whose knots were never counted draws nothing.
